summary: The supplied source bodies show a possible path from code_qa through repository readiness, index loading, FastCode.query, retrieval, generation, and optional session persistence. This is a static map, not evidence that the read-only sample ran, that its indexes are valid, or that an adaptation would work.

conclusions.text: code_qa calls _ensure_repos_ready, then _ensure_loaded, and returns an error string if either reports failure. It passes the resulting repository names to FastCode.query as repo_filter. FastCode.query separately rejects queries when repo_indexed is false; that check is outside its exception handler. The bodies of both readiness helpers and the code that sets repo_indexed were not supplied.

When the retriever has agency mode enabled and an iterative agent exists, FastCode.query constructs a minimal ProcessedQuery instead of calling query_processor.process. Otherwise it calls query_processor.process with dialogue summaries and LLM enhancement requested. It then calls retriever.retrieve and answer_generator.generate. This branch condition does not inspect the per-call use_agency_mode argument, although that argument is passed to retrieve; without retrieve's body, their interaction cannot be settled.

The supplied agency helper reconstructs a ProcessedQuery and calls iterative_agent.retrieve_with_iteration; it returns the original results if the agent is absent or the helper catches an exception. The supplied standard-retrieval helper instead calls semantic search, optional pseudocode search, keyword search, combination, reranking, and diversification before limiting results. Its general-filters stage is commented out. These helpers establish possible callee behavior, not which branch retrieve actually takes.

Semantic search embeds the search text, uses a nonempty filtered vector store when available or the full store otherwise, passes repo_filter to the store, and additionally checks returned repository names when repo_filter is set. Separate helpers implement language, type, and path filtering and a final repository filter, but their supplied bodies do not establish that retrieve calls them. In particular, the supplied standard-retrieval helper does not apply its general filters.

FastCode.query gives generation the original question, retrieved elements, processed-query information, full dialogue history from _get_full_dialogue_history, and an optional prompt_builder. It gives retrieval recent summaries instead. The supplied _truncate_context delegates to truncate_to_tokens, but no supplied generate body establishes whether or how it builds and truncates this context.

code_qa gets a FastCode instance, creates an eight-character UUID-derived session ID if none was provided, and passes that ID even when multi_turn is false. FastCode.query loads recent summaries only when both multi-turn mode and a session ID are present, but attempts to save a dialogue turn whenever a session ID is present. Thus the caller selects the session ID and repository filter, while FastCode.query owns the shown history lookup and save attempt.

FastCode.query disables query-result caching in the shown body. For a session, it extracts the generated answer, summary, and formatted sources, converts source and metadata values to JSON-serializable forms, and calls cache_manager.save_dialogue_turn. It ignores that method's boolean return and logs a saved turn regardless. save_dialogue_turn returns false when caching is disabled or an exception is caught; it does not check the return of its internal set call before returning true.

Index readiness involves distinct in-memory and filesystem evidence: FastCode.query checks repo_indexed, while the supplied _is_repo_indexed helper checks only for a named FAISS file and metadata file. File existence alone does not establish that an index loads or matches the active FastCode instance. The supplied BM25 loader can separately return false for a missing file or caught loading error.

Inside its try block, FastCode.query converts exceptions into a dictionary containing answer, query, and error. Its initial not-indexed RuntimeError is outside that block. code_qa reads answer and sources from the returned dictionary without checking error, and appends a session ID; a returned text response therefore does not prove successful retrieval or generation.

The supplied non-streaming OpenAI and Anthropic helpers return an error string when their client is absent, but raise caught provider or response-validation exceptions again. The streaming helpers instead yield error text for an absent client or caught exception. A consumer must not treat all returned or yielded text as a successful answer; the supplied bodies do not show how generate interprets these outcomes.

The iterative-agent bodies define adaptive iteration and line budgets and stopping checks for confidence, iteration count, line count, stagnation, and estimated cost. The standard-retrieval helper caps its result list at retriever.max_results. These are source-level limits, not proof that every possible query follows those paths. No supplied body establishes an end-to-end input length or generation prompt-size limit.

Loading a local repository is not inherently read-only: load_from_path either uses the directory directly when it is already at the workspace destination, or prepares a destination and copies the working tree, including untracked files, with symlinks preserved. Preparing an occupied destination calls a backup helper. Index persistence can write FAISS and metadata files. The backup helper's behavior and the exact loading/indexing path used by the sample are not supplied.

For incremental indexing, index_files reads each supplied file, skips it if content or parse_file returns None, indexes parsed elements, and generates embeddings for accumulated elements. A supplied parser fragment handles C/C++ class or struct and function node types, and a call-extractor helper accommodates dictionary or list capture formats. These fragments do not establish the complete supported-language set, parse_file behavior, or compatibility with the installed parser versions.

The supplied entry points offer distinct navigation boundaries: api.py and web_app.py each expose load-and-index routes, while mcp_server.py exposes code_qa and a force-reindex route. They must not be treated as one verified deployment or substituted for missing helper definitions. The supplied coverage reports 81 parsed files, 40 skipped files, and zero failed files out of 121 counted files; that is source-coverage information, not execution or test evidence.

unknowns: The bodies of _ensure_repos_ready, _ensure_loaded, index_repository, the code setting repo_indexed, and the complete retriever.retrieve implementation were not supplied; actual readiness and branch selection cannot be verified.

The bodies of QueryProcessor.process, AnswerGenerator.generate, prompt construction, _get_full_dialogue_history, and truncate_to_tokens were not supplied; effective input and context limits remain unverified.

The complete parser initialization, language registry, parse_file implementation, and dependency versions were not supplied; full parser support and static syntax compatibility cannot be established from these excerpts.
No test entry point or test result was supplied. No target code was executed, so compilation, persistence, retrieval isolation, generation quality, and runtime compatibility remain unverified.
